gp.heading: Gross profit
gp.text:
Gross profit as a percentage of revenue declined 220 basis points to 20.5% for the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. The decline was primarily driven by revenue shifts toward our lower-margin staffing businesses, specifically the outsized growth in PeopleReady energy work, which resulted in 190 basis points of contraction. Higher workers’ compensation costs contributed the remaining 30 basis points of contraction.

Gross profit as a percentage of revenue declined 280 basis points to 20.4% for the thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. Changes in revenue mix resulted in 130 basis points of contraction, primarily driven by revenue shifts toward our lower-margin staffing businesses. Higher workers’ compensation costs, driven by less favorable workers’ compensation reserve adjustments, resulted in 120 basis points of contraction. Additionally, the thirty-nine weeks ended September 28, 2025 included a benefit for recognition of certain COVID-19 government subsidies, contributing the remaining 30 basis points of contraction for the thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2026.

ga.text: • Total Company selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expense declined 2.9% to $89.1 million, compared to $91.7 million.

sga.text: • Total Company selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expense declined 2.9% to $89.1 million, compared to $91.7 million.

da_op.text: Depreciation and amortization decreased for the thirteen and thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2026, compared to the same periods in the prior year, primarily due to certain assets becoming fully depreciated during 2025.

nonop.text: We evaluate performance based on segment revenue and segment profit. Segment revenue is net of intercompany eliminations. Segment profit includes revenue, related cost of services, and ongoing operating expenses directly attributable to the reportable segment. Segment profit excludes loss on assets held-for-sale, goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges, depreciation and amortization expense, unallocated corporate general and administrative expense, interest and other income (expense), income taxes, and other costs and benefits not considered to be ongoing. See Note 13: Segment Information , to our consolidated financial statements found in Item 1 of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, for additional details on our reportable segments, as well as a reconciliation of segment profit to income (loss) before tax expense.

tax.text: Our tax provision and our effective tax rate are subject to variation due to several factors, including variability in accurately predicting our full-year pre-tax income or loss by jurisdiction, tax credits, government audit developments, changes in laws, regulations and administrative practices, valuation allowances recorded on deferred tax assets, and relative changes in expenses or losses for which tax benefits are not recognized. Additionally, our effective tax rate can be more or less volatile based on the amount of pre-tax income or loss. For example, the impact of discrete items, tax credits, and non-deductible expenses on our effective tax rate is greater when our pre-tax income or loss is lower.

net.text: • The items above resulted in net income of $9.2 million, compared to net loss of $1.9 million.

ocf.heading: Cash flows from operating activities
ocf.text:
Operating cash flows consist of net loss adjusted for non-cash benefits and expenses, and changes in operating assets and liabilities.

As client demand improves, the result is generally an increase in accounts receivable and accounts payable. Accrued wages and benefits can fluctuate based on whether the period end requires the accrual of one or two weeks of payroll, the amount and timing of bonus payments, and the timing of payroll tax payments.

Net cash used by accounts receivable during the thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2026 was primarily due to an increase in revenue coupled with an increase in days sales outstanding of approximately four days compared to the fiscal fourth quarter of 2025, both reflecting shifts in revenue and corresponding receivables mix toward clients with longer payment terms. In addition, our workers’ compensation claims reserve for estimated claims decreased over the period, driven by prior-year claim payments.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization decreased for the thirteen and thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2026, compared to the same periods in the prior year, primarily due to certain assets becoming fully depreciated during 2025.

wc.text: Cash generated through our core operations is generally our primary source of liquidity. Our principal ongoing cash needs are to finance working capital, fund capital expenditures, repay outstanding Amended Revolving Credit Facility balances, and execute share repurchases. We may also need cash to fund future acquisitions. We manage working capital through timely collection of accounts receivable, which we achieve through focused collection efforts and close monitoring of trends in days sales outstanding. While client payment terms are generally 90 days or less, we pay our associates daily and weekly, so additional financing through the use of our Amended Revolving Credit Facility is necessary to support working capital needs in times of revenue growth. We also manage working capital through efficient cost management and the strategic timing of accounts payable payments.

capex.text: Investing cash flows consist of capital expenditures, business acquisitions, and purchases, sales, and maturities of restricted investments, which are managed in line with our workers’ compensation collateral funding requirements and timing of claim payments.

net sales.heading: Revenue from services
net sales.text: Total Company revenue grew 20.7% to $520.7 million for the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2026, and grew 13.7% to $1.4 billion for the thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2026, compared to the same periods in the prior year. The increase in revenue was primarily driven by growth within our skilled businesses, specifically in the energy and commercial driving industries, as well as growth in our core, on-demand business and permanent placements. Growth was partially offset by declines within our OnSite and healthcare staffing businesses, as demand continued to stabilize within these offerings.

lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our ten largest clients accounted for 26.2% of total revenue for fiscal 2025, 22.4% for fiscal 2024 and 20.5% for fiscal 2023.
Our success as a company depends on our ability to attract, develop and retain talented employees.

During challenging economic times or in the event of a reduction or elimination of government funding, our clients, including but not limited to those that rely on government support, may face reduced demand for their services, reduced revenue, and issues gaining access to sufficient credit, which has resulted in and could in the future result in a reduction in the need for our services, or an impairment of their ability to make payments to us, timely or otherwise, for services rendered.

Our clients increasingly rely on automation, AI, machine learning and other new technologies to reduce their dependence on labor needs, which may reduce demand for our staffing and recruiting services and impact our operations.
In addition, our business relies on a variety of technologies, including those that support recruiting, hiring, paying, order management, billing, collecting, and associate and client data analytics.
For some solutions, we depend on key vendors and partners to provide technology and support.

The timing and amount of the repurchases, if any, will be determined at management’s discretion and depend upon several factors, including market and business conditions, the trading price of our common stock and the nature of other investment opportunities.
Our principal sources of liquidity are funds generated from operating activities, available cash and cash equivalents, and borrowings under our Revolving Credit Facility.

We rely on information technology systems to process, transmit, and store electronic information and to communicate among our locations around the world and with our clients, vendors, associates and employees.
We rely on our information technology systems to monitor and control our operations, adjust to changing market conditions, implement strategic initiatives and provide services to clients.

We currently use and may, in the future, further rely on AI, which introduces certain risks including dependency on accurate AI performance, potential data privacy and security breaches, challenges in regulatory compliance, ethical considerations, potential workforce disruption, the risk of intellectual property infringement and emerging technology risks.

Our associate and customer engagement on mobile devices depends upon third parties maintaining open application marketplaces and effective operation with mobile operating systems, networks, and standards that we do not control.

Our application relies on third-party open application store platforms, including the Apple App Store and Google Play, which may change their policies, impose additional fees or requirements to support our applications, or stop supporting our applications altogether.

Our success depends upon our ability to attract, onboard, develop and retain a sufficient number of qualified employees, including management, sales, recruiting, service, technology and administrative personnel.
We depend on the efforts of our executive officers and certain key personnel.
Cash generated through our core operations is generally our primary source of liquidity.
